findings.title: audible join: listen.mp3 + k.mp3 + k.mp3
findings.detail: The speaker says the letter name 'kay' (/keɪ/) twice instead of producing the target pure phoneme /k/. (judge 0/10; heard: lɪsən... kʰeɪ, kʰeɪ)

findings.title: audible join: t_but_in_this_word.mp3 + th.mp3
findings.detail: The target sound /θ/ has an audible plosive onset and sounds like 'tfs' rather than a clean, pure voiceless dental fricative. (judge 3/10; heard: bət ɪn ðɪs wɜːd ɪts [tfsː])

findings.title: audible join: dojo_find.mp3 + ae.mp3
findings.detail: The recording provides the letter name /eɪ/ rather than the target short vowel sound /æ/, and the final sound has an unnatural pause and drop in energy, making it sound pasted in. (judge 4/10; heard: kæn juː faɪnd eɪ)

findings.title: audible join: thats.mp3 + w.mp3
findings.detail: The target sound is pronounced as 'woo' with a prominent vowel rather than a pure /w/ phoneme, though the voice match and acoustic environment are consistent. (judge 4/10; heard: ðæts wuː)

findings.title: audible join: dojo_find.mp3 + ks.mp3
findings.detail: The recording join and acoustics are seamless, but the speaker pronounces the letter name 'x' (/ɛks/) instead of the pure phoneme /ks/. (judge 6/10; heard: kən juː faɪnd ɛks)

findings.title: audible join: listen.mp3 + ks.mp3
findings.detail: The transition and acoustics are relatively smooth, but the teacher pronounces the letter name 'x' (/ɛks/) instead of the target pure sound /ks/. (judge 6/10; heard: ˈlɪsən... ɛks)
